protocol.name: gex_glass_v1
protocol.copyright: Copyright 2026 the gex authors. Same terms as the rest of gex.
protocol.description:
Windows 7 draws Aero's glass in its compositor (DWM): parts of a window show what is beneath them, blurred and tinted with the colorization colour. A Win32 window asks for it with DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea and DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow, and its glass frame is glass as well. Here the client names those parts of a surface; the compositor fills them with the blurred backdrop and draws the surface's own pixels over it, alpha blended, as DWM does.
State takes effect at once, like gex_window_placement_v1's: a window changing its glass does not need new contents.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Glass objects already made are unaffected.

request.name: get_glass
request.description: The surface has no glass until a region is set.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface is drawn as an ordinary one.

request.name: set_region
request.description: In surface coordinates; null is the whole surface, an empty region no glass. The region is copied as it is now. A compositor may keep only a few rectangles of it, and the bounds of the rest.

request.name: set_colorization
request.description: DWM's colorization parameters (Windows 7's ColorizationColor, ColorizationColorBalance, ColorizationBlurBalance, ColorizationAfterglow, ColorizationAfterglowBalance): the glass is the blurred backdrop times blur_balance, plus the colour times balance, plus the afterglow colour times the backdrop's brightness times afterglow_balance; balances 0 to 100.

entry.name: frame
entry.summary: draw Windows 7's frame on the glass

request.name: set_frame
request.description: What DWM draws on a window's glass frame: the frame itself, and the caption buttons where the client's window system has them (it hit tests them, so they are drawn where it says), and the client area: outside it, as under DWM, the frame is drawn over the surface and the surface's own pixels do not show. Rectangles are in surface coordinates. The caption text is the surface's title.
